schemes.english_name: Entrepreneurship and Innovation Consultancy Project (MSc, Henley Business School)
schemes.description: Postgraduate summer capstone in which student consultancy teams practise on case studies then work for a real host entrepreneur from mid-June to late July, meeting the host face to face and online; teams present their analysis and each student writes a project proposal sent to the host entrepreneur.
schemes.admin_host: Henley Business School (Digitalisation, Marketing and Entrepreneurship)
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: MSc Entrepreneurship and Innovation (programme specification treats MMM161 as the dissertation equivalent); other programmes using the module not verified
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Master's-level (Level 7) module; programme eligibility beyond MSc Entrepreneurship and Innovation not verified.
schemes.credit_assessment: 40 credits, Level 7. 2025/6: Task 1 individual self-assessment 20%; Task 2 team oral presentation 30%; Task 3 individual 5,000-word proposal for the host entrepreneur 50%.
schemes.duration: Teams work with host mid-June to late July; module runs Semester 2/Summer (Task 3 due Week 12)
schemes.delivery_format: In-person and online team meetings and host visits; convenor monitors attendance
schemes.project_evidence: Source 2: live consultancy for a real entrepreneur, 'not a case study'; outputs are team presentation and written project proposal for the host (source 1).
schemes.group_evidence: Sources 1-2: consultancy team works with its project host; assessed 25-minute team presentation (30%). Individual proposals are also assessed, but teamwork on the live project is documented.
schemes.employer_evidence: Source 2: students work for real entrepreneurs (project hosts) who interact with the team and receive the individual proposals; 2023/4 and earlier versions also had a client-facing team report. The team presentation itself is delivered to the convenor, not the client.
schemes.partner_role: Host entrepreneurs supply the venture/problem, meet the team and receive written proposals.
schemes.deliverable: Team presentation; individual project proposal for the host entrepreneur
schemes.unresolved: Programmes taking the module beyond MSc Entrepreneurship and Innovation, and whether it is compulsory vs optional elsewhere, not verified. Host entrepreneurs' sectors and names not published. Assessment structure changed between 2024/5 and 2025/6.

profile_md:
Reading's documented employer-linked group provision is concentrated in postgraduate taught programmes in Henley Business School and the Economics group, with a few undergraduate leads.

**Qualifying routes (current 2025/26 evidence):** (1) MMM161 Entrepreneurship and Innovation Consultancy Project (40 credits, MSc Entrepreneurship and Innovation), where teams work with a real host entrepreneur over June-July and each student writes a proposal for the host; (2) ECM200 Capstone Project (20 credits), where small supervised teams produce a report/presentation for an external organisation (businesses, government agencies, NGOs, start-ups) across MSc Economics-family and Public Policy programmes; (3) REMF56 Real Estate Opportunities, whose Industry Challenge (40% of the module) has teams respond to an industry partner's brief and present to that partner.

**Partial evidence:** Henley's MMM190 (MSc Management) and MMM194 (MSc International Business) consulting projects and the Executive MBA team projects name organisations but do not show team structure or delivery year. Typography's Real Jobs live briefs are real-client but described as one-on-one. Food Technology's New Product Development is team-based with an industry-expert brief, and Going Public (Archaeology and History) is a group project for external partners, but partner identity is unclear. The Construction Live Project is a team build with partner-contractor support but no client brief.

**Scope:** All routes are programme-specific, mostly optional or tied to a master's programme; no institution-wide scheme exists (RED Awards and the Reading Internship Scheme are award-based or individual). Participation numbers are unpublished. Named partners are not published.
gaps: Searched with ~39 queries via search-index only. Unverified: group structure and delivery year for MMM190, MMM194, Executive MBA projects; whether MMM161 is compulsory in programmes beyond MSc Entrepreneurship and Innovation; partner identity for Food NPD and Going Public; individual vs team split for Typography Real Jobs; engineering/computing (further Built Environment client modules e.g. CE2CPR, Real Estate undergraduate projects), Pharmacy/Chemistry/Biological Sciences/Meteorology, Education, Film/Theatre/Art, MSc Environmental Management expert-panel contaminated-site project (clients from industry on panel) and other Henley PG programmes were not searched in depth; further departmental instances likely.
